title: Pneumonia, lung abscess, empyema and respiratory arrest in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the main lung condition (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/18/2026
Reason for Admission: Community-acquired pneumonia

Vitals:
Temperature: 101.2 F (on admission)
Blood Pressure: 128/82 mmHg
Heart Rate: 88 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 20 breaths/min
Oxygen Saturation: 94% on room air

Recent Labs:
WBC count: 14,500 cells/mcL
Hemoglobin: 12.4 g/dL
Platelets: 210,000/mcL
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
eGFR: 72 mL/min/1.73m2
Sputum Culture: Positive for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA)

Review of Systems:
The patient reports productive cough with yellow sputum, shortness of breath, and generalized malaise. She denies chest pain, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss. She denies any recent travel or known exposure to contagious illnesses.

Social History:
The patient is a retired teacher who lives at home with her spouse. She denies current tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History:
Mother had hypertension and diabetes. Father had a history of stroke.

Hospital Course:
The patient is a 77-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department with a three-day history of productive cough and fever. Upon examination, she was febrile with crackles noted in the right lower lobe. She was admitted for the management of pneumonia. A sputum culture was obtained, which identified a methicillin-resistant organism. Based on these results, she was started on intravenous vancomycin. She remained stable on the floor, showing clinical improvement in oxygenation and a decreasing temperature over five days. She tolerated the treatment well and was transitioned to oral medications prior to discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Pneumonia
MRSA infection

Discharge Medications:
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875mg every 8 hours
Acetaminophen 650mg every 6 hours as needed for fever
Guaifenesin 600mg every 4 hours as needed for cough

Follow-up:
The patient will follow up with her primary care physician in one week for a repeat physical examination and a review of her progress.

Electronically signed,
E. Castillo, MD
05/18/2026
refs: ICD-10-CM Tabular: J15-J18, J69, J85-J86, R09
